propositions: Canonical preview/sync routes must emit only exit codes 0/1/2 for benign/paused/success/operational-failure/invalid-config states respectively, while legacy reconcile routes retain historical 3/4/75 numeric translations for another-live-pass/phase-gate/reschedule.

Both canonical and legacy adapters consume a single typed disposition result and preserve identical repository/ref mutation semantics and paused commit-skip behavior without introducing retry or cache seams.
Legacy CLI, direct-engine, Python facade, and MCP bridge consumers must operate without a numeric whitelist; production workflows must use canonical 0/1/2 only with no old-code compatibility case.

Deployment automation, systemd units, Jenkins jobs, and existing scripts consuming or checking 3/4/75 must either be migrated to canonical 0/1/2 or explicitly classified as legacy-compatibility-only in tests and documentation.
All three numeric-consumer inventory, documentation, and code-boundary verification criteria must be complete with measurable evidence before merge gate approval.
